q: 1. The paper size of A4 is
explain: As per ISO 216 A-series standard, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 2. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such as A4, A3, A2 … is
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: The A-series is designed so length:width = √2:1, i.e. the width is 1/√2 times the length, preserving the aspect ratio when the sheet is halved.

q: 3. In the engineering system of paper sizes, which of the following is "A2" size?
4. A typical layout of drawing sheet do not contain .............
explain: Standard drawing sheet layouts include centering marks, orientation marks, and identification/title marks, but 'trimming marks' are not part of the standard sheet layout elements defined by drawing standards.

q: 5. The paper size of A3 is
explain: Standard ISO paper sizes: A3 is 297mm x 420mm (double the size of A4).

q: 6. Number of orientation mark generally contained by a drawing sheet is .............
explain: A standard drawing sheet layout generally includes two orientation marks to indicate the correct viewing direction of the sheet.

q: 7. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A2 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^2$), A0 is four times the size of A2.

q: 8. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A4 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^4$), A0 is sixteen times the size of A4.

q: 9. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begain from
explain: Filling tables from bottom upward leaves room at the top for later entries, allowing the table to be extended easily.

q: 10. When only one drawing is to be made then its position should be .............
explain: A single drawing on a sheet is conventionally positioned at the centre of the paper for balanced composition and to leave adequate margins on all sides.

q: 11. Size of letter means the ............. of the letter.
explain: In lettering standards, the 'size' of a letter refers to its height, which determines the overall scale/legibility of the lettering on a drawing.

q: 12. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is .............
explain: As per drawing standards, the standard title block size used uniformly across all drawing sheet sizes is 185 mm × 65 mm.

q: 13. Title block gives the information about:
explain: The title block consolidates all key drawing information: title, scale, serial/sheet number, and more.

q: 14. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such A4, A3, A2 ..... is .............
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: Since the A-series maintains a length:width ratio of √2:1, the width equals the length divided by √2, i.e., 1/√2 times the length.

q: 15. What is the standard size (in mm) of A3 size drawing sheet?
explain: As per ISO A-series, A3 measures 297 mm × 420 mm.

q: 16. The 'title block' is provided in a drawing sheet at:
explain: By drafting convention the title block is placed in the bottom-right hand corner of the sheet for easy reference when folded.

q: 17. The preparation of a successful drawing depends on the ............. of drawing sheet.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'letters' is marked correct — implying that clear, standardized lettering/notation is emphasized as central to a successful, communicative drawing.

q: 18. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about
explain: The title block consolidates the drawing title, scale and serial/sheet number along with other reference details.

q: 19. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size (in mm) is
explain: A board of about 1500 × 1000 × 25 mm is large enough to accommodate an A0 sheet (841 × 1189 mm) with margins.

q: 20. Title book of drawing sheet contains
explain: The title block contains all key reference details: drawing title, drawing number and scale, among others.

q: 21. The selection of suitable scale and allotment of proper space for margin, title block, revision panel, folding marks, etc. on the drawing sheet is known as :
explain: Layout refers to the organized arrangement of all required elements on a drawing sheet.

q: 22. Building working drawing are generally prepared in drawing paper of:
explain: Building working drawings, which need to show adequate detail for large structures, are generally prepared on A1 size sheets.

q: 23. The paper size is
explain: 297 × 420 mm corresponds to the standard A3 sheet size, matching the correct option given.

q: 24. The size of A2 size paper is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A2 measures 420 mm × 594 mm.

q: 25. Most prevailing size of drawing sheets used in preparation of municipal drawing for building permit is .............
explain: Municipal building permit drawings are commonly prepared and submitted on A1 size sheets, balancing detail and manageable size for official records.

q: 26. The following is not included in title block of drawing sheet
explain: The title block typically records sheet number, scale, and sheet size, but the method of projection is shown separately (often via a projection symbol), not as a standard title block entry.

q: 27. ............. maximum tangents can be drawn from an outside point on a circle.
explain: From any point located outside a circle, exactly two distinct tangent lines can be drawn to the circle, touching it at two separate points.

q: 28. The title block is provided in a drawing sheet at .............
explain: As per standard drawing sheet layout conventions, the title block is placed in the bottom right-hand corner of the sheet for easy identification when the sheet is folded or filed.

q: 29. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about .............
explain: The title block consolidates key reference information — drawing title, scale, drawing number, and other details — making 'all of these' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 30. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of .............
explain: A concept drawing represents the initial design idea and is prepared before construction begins, to communicate and finalize the overall design intent.
